paragraph_content.content: The hot deformation behavior of low-density high-strength FeeMneAleC steel at T 900

is studied using the Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator. The rheological stress curve characteristics of the steel are analyzed through experimental data and the dynamic recrystallization activation energy is calculated. The critical strain/stress, peak strain/stress and steady-state strain/stress models of dynamic recrystallization are characterized by introducing the dimensionless parameter Zener-Hollomon. The microstructure evolution is analyzed and the dynamic recrystallization state diagram of the steel is drawn. The results indicated that the steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and a positive strain rate-sensitive material. The dynamic recrystallization activation energy is 669.844 kJ mol<sup>1</sup>. With the decrease of <sup>ε</sup>_ or the increase of T, the Z parameter decreases gradually and the dynamic recrystallization behavior is more likely to occur; however, its grain size increases accordingly. The fine and uniform grain structure can be obtained by hot working in the range of

. Finally, the prediction model for the dynamic recrystallization average grain size is established, and the correlation coefficient (R) of the prediction model is 0.996; therefore, the model has a high prediction accuracy.

paragraph_content.content: With the rapid development of the automobile industry, automotive lightweight materials have become an important research topic. Among them, FeeMneAleC steel has good corrosion resistance, low density and excellent comprehensive mechanical properties, having great application prospect in the fields of weight reduction, collision safety and the complex working conditions of the automobiles structure [1e4]. In addition, thermoplastic deformation can effectively refine the grain size and improve the properties of forgings and microstructure. In the field of actual production, the microstructure is primarily controlled by way of thermal machining. Dynamic recrystallization (DRX) is beneficial to grain refinement and homogenization and is an important deformation mechanism to improve the microstructure and properties within the hot working process [5e7]. Therefore, in-depth studies on the microstructure evolution and DRX behavior of FeeMneAleC steel are of great significance for the formulation and optimization of the hot forging process of the steel.

At present, reports on FeeMneAleC steel primarily focus on smelting, heat treatment and mechanical properties. For example, Moon et al. [8] studied Fee30Mn-10.5Al-1.1C-(0e5) Mo steel. It was found that Mo-enriched

carbides precipitate during the solution treatment when the Mo content is higher than 4%, inhibiting the growth of the austenite grains during the solution treatment. Liu et al. [9] heated Fee11Mne10Al-1.25C steel and cooled the steel via three different methods. It was found that the distribution of -carbide in the samples after intense cooling was more uniform than that of the samples after air and water cooling; this, the corresponding mechanical properties were superior. However, the research reports on the hot deformation behavior of low-density high-strength FeeMneAleC steel are not thorough enough. In this paper, the microstructure evolution law and DRX behavior of the steel were studied using a thermal simulation compression experiment and metallographic observation. The flow stress curve characteristics of the steel were analyzed through the experimental data, and the dynamic recrystallization activation energy and Z parameters were calculated. The critical strain conditions for DRX were determined based on the Cingara-McQueen equation [10]. Functional relationships between rheological stress curve characteristic values (critical strain/stress, peak strain/ stress and steady-state strain/stress) and the dimensionless parameter Zener-Hollomon [11] were established. A dynamic recrystallization state diagram was drawn and a dynamic recrystallization average grain size prediction model was constructed. The research results provide theoretical support for the determination of the hot forging processes parameters as well as the numerical simulation of the hot forming of lowdensity high-strength Fe-Mn-Al-C steel

Zener and Hollomon [11] studied the constitutive relationship of steel and found that rheological stress depends on temperature and strain rate. Therefore, they proposed the Zener-Hollomon (Z) parameter model to characterize the comprehensive influence of T and <sup>ε</sup>_ on the rheological stress.

The temperature compensated strain rate function (Z parameter formula (3)) has been applied in many studies. Singh et al. [18] studied the dynamic recrystallization of a high Nb-containing cast -TiAl based Tie45Ale8Nbe2Cr-0.2B alloy during hot compressive deformation and analyzed the Zener-Hollomon parameter modulated recrystallization mechanisms. Wang et al. [19] conducted the constitutive analysis of as-cast 40CrNiMo alloy steel through isothermal compression experiments and established the Arrhenius-type constitutive equation with the Zener-Hollomon parameter, having excellent accuracy. Detrois et al. [20] studied the hot deformation behavior of a Ni-based superalloy and simulated the flow stress from the experimental data using the Zener-Hollomon parameter.

paragraph_content.content: LevenbergeMarquardt optimization algorithm was used to perform the mathematical regression analysis on the experimental data, and the prediction model for the average grain size of the dynamic recrystallization of the low-density highstrength steel was obtained:

In order to verify the accuracy of the prediction model, the correlation analysis and error test of the predicted value of the grain size and the experimental value were carried out. The accuracy of the chosen model can be assessed through the following two parameters: R and MRE. They can be defined as:
represent the experiment data of the testing and the corresponding predicted data acquired from the model; n is the number of testing data; M and N are the average values of

respectively. The correlation coefficient (R) was usually used to show the linear relations between the predicted and the experimental data. To evaluate the selected model, the average relative error (MRE) was considered an unbiased statistic for confirming the credibility of the model.

During the dynamic recrystallization of the material, the grain size constantly changes under the driving force. On the one hand, the grain growth is promoted under the action of temperature and plastic strain and the driving force has a positive effect on the grain size. On the other hand, dynamic recrystallization refines the microstructure inside the material and the driving force is a counter-driving force, which inhibits the grain growth [27e29]. This may cause errors in the dynamic recrystallization average grain size prediction model. In addition, there were some statistical errors. The results are shown in Fig. 11, R is 0.996 and MRE for all samples is only 4.53%, indicating a high degree of coincidence. Figure 11 (c) shows that the absolute error between the predicted value of the grain size and the experimental value is mostly within 3 m, which further shows that the model can accurately predict the dynamic recrystallization average grain size of low-density high-strength steel. It provides a reliable theoretical basis for the prediction of the dynamic recrystallized grain size of the steel after hot forging.

When setting the experimental conditions, we considered different parameters and obtained the best value of each parameter. Using multivariate research (experimental design and chemometrics), optimizing of two or more parameters is easier, more statistically correct and functional. At present, this multivariate method (experimental design) has been used in other studies (such as energy, environment and sensors). Hendriksen et al. [30] expanded the application of Noise2- Inverse in space, time and spectrum-like domains based on convolutional neural networks. <sup>þ</sup> ratio and xanthan gum dosage on the overall photovoltaic parameters of laboratory-scale solar cells at a multivariate level. Miccoli et al. [32] presented an efficient multisensor based on a single zinc oxide microwire/gold junction. The device can detect in real time three different stimuli, UV-VIS light, temperature and pH variations. It shows great potential for use in the field of biosensors. Yun et al. [33] used headspace vaporized GC/MS (HS-GC/MS) to analyze black tea samples collected from 10 geographic origins. The findings support the use of HS-GC/MS combined with chemometrics as a tool to identify the origin of black tea. Galliano et al. [34] have adopted an experimental strategy of multivariate chemometric approach to study the main factors influencing dye-sensitized solar cells efficiency and stability and obtained an optimized system which can improve their efficiency. Bella et al. [35] proposed the replacement of the liquid electrolyte with quasi-linear polymer electrolyte membranes, with the aim of increasing the durability of the device. The experimental conditions are investigated and optimized by means of a multivariate chemometric approach, and the characterization of the materials and devices was presented.

In conclusion, we will carry out the multivariate study in future work in order to take into account all the relevant variables and their interactions, finding the best experimental conditions for the proper functioning of their materials/devices/reactors.
